Q: How can I efficiently check if an element exists more than once in an array? A:

Adding and removing elements doesn't seem very efficient. Looking up an item in a set is O(1) (constant time), so simply checking if i in seen is much faster than modifying the set structure repeatedly.

If you only need to know if any element is repeated, you can do:

has_duplicates = len(nums) != len(set(nums))

If you need to know exactly which one is repeated:

from collections import Counter

counts = Counter(nums)
duplicates = [item for item, count in counts.items() if count > 1]

print(duplicates) # Output: [3, 2]

Both options are O(n).

Q: How to save dpi info in py-opencv? A:

To add the DPI information (actually pixels per meter) without external lib, and if you are sure the pHYs chunk is not already in the file, you can just insert the right chunk directly in the file headers:


import binascii

with open("image.png", "r+b") as f:
    PNG_SIGNATURE = b'\x89\x50\x4e\x47\x0D\x0A\x1A\x0A'
    data = f.read()
    if not data.startswith(PNG_SIGNATURE):
        raise ValueError("Not a PNG image")

    # pHYs chunk (https://www.libpng.org/pub/png/spec/1.2/png-1.2-pdg.html#C.pHYs)
    ppu = int(dots_per_inch * 39.370079).to_bytes(4, "big")
    unit = int(1).to_bytes(1)    # use meters
    c_type = b"pHYs"
    c_data = ppu + ppu + unit
    c_csum = binascii.crc32(c_type + c_data).to_bytes(4, "big")
    phys = len(c_data).to_bytes(4, "big") + c_type + c_data + c_csum

    # just insert the pHYs chunk after the IHDR (4 + 4 + 13 + 4)
    PHYS_OFF = len(PNG_SIGNATURE) + 25
    f.seek(PHYS_OFF)
    f.write(phys)
    f.write(data[PHYS_OFF:])

It is then possible to check the modified file with pngcheck:

pngcheck -v image.png | grep pHYs

or Image Magick:

identify -units PixelsPerInch -format '%[fx:int(resolution.x)]x%[fx:int(resolution.y)]\n' image.png

Q: Vim74: E149 Sorry no help for help.txt A:

You can get the same “E149 Sorry no help for help.txt” error if you have a long-running Vim session and the Vim program files were upgraded in the meantime.

This happened to me: I had started an editing session in a GNU screen window on my Debian testing system using Vim 8.1. Some time later, unattenttended-upgrades upgraded Vim 8.1 to 8.2 with the result that the run-time paths were now no longer valid. I could have saved the session and restarted Vim, but it was simpler/easier to run the following command (specific to 8.2):

:set helpfile=/usr/share/vim/vim82/doc/help.txt

Q: Aggregate a column in `i` in a join using `by = .EACHI` A:

The comments are good, here's a method to get your desired 4, 8, 10 values:

sum(v) using by=.EACHI is going to see only one value of v each, since this is done before v is expanded by the join process. While I'm not sure why this is done before, my guess (without looking at the code) is either efficiency or convenience, neither of which may seem satisfying in this use. I suspect that it may be related to the fact that there will be one row output for each input-row of i, so therefore v will have only one observation within by=.EACHI.

However, just like sum(value) did what you expect, we can mimic the repeats of v by using length(value), as in

DT[i, v * length(value), by = .EACHI, on = "id"]
#        id    V1
#    <char> <num>
# 1:      a     4
# 2:      a     8
# 3:      b    10

We don't need sum since the .EACHI ensures we are really looking at one row from i at a time, so length(v) is always 1.
